pages.title: Authentication - Plain Docs
pages.text:
A machine user can have several API keys, so you can rotate them without downtime. Each API key carries its own fine-grained permissions.
To call the API as a user in your workspace, use an OAuth app.

1

Create a machine user

Go to **Settings → Machine users & agents** and click **Add machine user**. Pick **API User** and click **Continue**. Pick **Agent** instead if you’re building an agent.A machine user has two fields:

* **Name:** visible only to you and could indicate the usage e.g. “Autoresponder”
* **Public name:** This is the name visible to customers (if the machine user interacts with customers) e.g. “Mr Robot”

2

Create an API Key

Click “Add API key” and select the permissions you need. When making API calls, if you have insufficient permissions, the error should tell you which permissions you need.The relevant documentation will tell you which permissions are required for each feature.Once you’ve made an API key you should copy it and put it somewhere safe, as you will not be able to see it again once you navigate away.

3

Go build things 🚀

Now that you have an API key, pass it on any API call as a header:

```
Authorization: Bearer plainApiKey_xxx
```

pages.title: Set up Plain for a person - Plain Docs
pages.text:
You are an agent setting up Plain, a customer support platform, for the person you’re working with. You do the setup through Plain’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at `https://mcp.plain.com/mcp`, which signs in as that person with OAuth. Don’t ask the person for an API key: the MCP server needs none, and an API key belongs to a machine user, not to them.
Steps 1 through 4 establish the connection and where to resume. Before you make any change in step 5, tell the person exactly what you propose and wait for their approval.
When the person has to choose, use your host’s question tool if it has one, such as `AskUserQuestion` in Claude Code. Otherwise ask in chat.
Related resources:

* **MCP server reference**: MCP server lists every tool and host-specific troubleshooting
* **Docs index**: `https://www.plain.com/docs/llms.txt`
* **OAuth metadata**: `https://mcp.plain.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`

## 1. Check for an existing connection

If Plain tools are already loaded, call `getMyWorkspace`. If the person gave you a workspace ID, compare it with the returned ID. Otherwise, tell them the workspace name and ID and ask them to confirm. Go to step 4 once the workspace matches.
If you can’t verify the workspace, ask whether the person already has one unless they supplied a workspace ID (it starts with `w_`). Go to step 2 if they need to create a workspace. If they already have one and Plain is configured, have them sign out of the existing connection and authenticate again with the intended workspace. If Plain needs to be configured, go to step 3.

## 2. Have the person sign up and create a workspace

The person signs up themselves. You can’t create an account or a workspace for them. Send them this link and wait for them to say they’re done:

```
https://app.plain.com/get-started
```

Tell them to:

1. Sign up with Google or their work email
2. Name their workspace when Plain asks
3. Come back to you once the workspace exists

Don’t connect the MCP server before the workspace exists. The connection gets bound to an account with no workspace, every tool fails with `No workspace ID provided`, and the person has to reconnect.

## 3. Connect the Plain MCP server

If Plain is already configured, follow the reconnection instructions in step 1. Otherwise, add the server for the host you’re running in. The host opens a browser window for the person to sign in to Plain and pick the workspace. The person must finish that sign-in themselves.

### Claude Code

Run this command, then ask the person to run `/mcp`, select `plain`, and choose **Authenticate**:

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user plain https://mcp.plain.com/mcp
```

Claude Code loads the Plain tools once authentication finishes. If they don’t appear, ask the person to restart Claude Code.

### Codex

Run this command. Codex detects that the server uses OAuth and opens the browser sign-in:

```
codex mcp add plain --url https://mcp.plain.com/mcp
```

### Cursor

Add the server to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or to `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "plain": {
      "url": "https://mcp.plain.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Cursor shows a **Needs login** prompt next to Plain. Ask the person to click it.

### Claude and Claude desktop

You can’t add a connector from inside a chat. Ask the person to:

1. Go to **Customize** → **Connectors**
2. Click **+**, then **Add custom connector**
3. Name it `Plain` and set the URL to `https://mcp.plain.com/mcp`
4. Click **Connect** next to the new connector and sign in

On a Team or Enterprise plan, only an admin can add custom connectors. If the person isn’t an admin, they need to ask theirs.

### ChatGPT

Plain has an official ChatGPT plugin. Ask the person to:

1. Open the Plain plugin and add it
2. Sign in with their Plain account and choose the workspace

### Other hosts

Any host that supports remote MCP servers over HTTP with OAuth works. Point it at `https://mcp.plain.com/mcp`. If your host can’t connect to remote MCP servers, tell the person you can’t set up Plain from here and send them to Claude or ChatGPT with the steps above.
Once the person connects, verify the workspace as described in step 1.

## 4. Find where setup left off

Ask which setup screen the person sees. The prompt copied from **Set up with your agent** includes the workspace ID. The person already named the workspace, and they may have completed or skipped other steps.
If they closed the setup screen, ask them to reopen `https://app.plain.com/workspace/workspace_id_here/setup` and tell you what they see. Replace `workspace_id_here` with the verified ID from `getMyWorkspace` before sharing the link. If Plain opens the workspace instead, ask what they want help with and continue only with the tasks they request.

## 5. Help with the current setup step

Work through one screen at a time and honor any steps the person skips. Check what exists before proposing changes. If a write fails or its result is unclear, check what succeeded before trying again.


| Screen | How to help |
| --- | --- |
| **Add your logo** | Ask the person to upload their logo in Plain or click **Continue without a logo**. If the logo is already there, ask them to click **Continue**. |
| **Create your first labels** | Read the existing labels with `getLabels`. If `showLabels` is available and the host can display the view, pass `suggestions` so the person can choose which labels to create. Let the view show the suggestions. Otherwise, propose labels in chat and use `createLabelType` only for labels they approve. |
| **Set up Tiers and SLAs** | Read existing tiers with `tiers`. Help the person choose which tiers to add in Plain. If the screen offers a first-response service level agreement (SLA), help them choose a target or select **No SLA**. |
| **Add your knowledge sources** | Read existing sources with `knowledgeSources`. Ask which documentation URL they want Plain to index. They can add it in Plain, or you can use `createKnowledgeSource` for the URL they approve. Use type `SITEMAP` if the URL path ends in `.xml`, ignoring case, and `URL` otherwise. |
| **Which tools does your team use?** | Ask the person to select the tools their team uses in Plain and continue. This screen records preferences. Connecting tools can happen after setup. |
| **Try Plain with test threads** | If this screen appears, ask the person whether to generate test threads or click **Continue without test threads**. If test threads already exist, they can click **Continue**. |

After a change you make through MCP, tell the person what succeeded and ask them to return to the setup screen. If Plain still shows that step, have them refresh and use the on-screen button to continue. After the person completes a step in Plain, verify the result with a tool when you can and ask what they see next.

## 6. Finish in the Plain app

When the person reaches **Setup complete**, ask them to review the summary and click **Go to your workspace**. Summarize what you set up and what they chose to skip. If the **Get started** checklist appears in their workspace, they can use it for follow-up tasks such as connecting Slack or inviting their team.

## If something fails

| Error | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `No workspace ID provided` | Have the person reconnect as described in step 1. If they need a workspace first, follow step 2. |
| `403` after OAuth completes | The token is missing the `openid offline_access` scopes. Have the person disconnect and reconnect the MCP server. If your host lets you set scopes, request both. |
| A tool is missing | The host cached an old tool list. Disconnect and reconnect the MCP server. |
| A permission error | The person’s role in Plain doesn’t allow that action. An admin can do it, or change their role. |
| Anything else | Tell the person to email help@plain.com with their workspace ID, the error, and the host they’re using. |

# Plain: agentic infrastructure for B2B customer support
> Plain is the agentic infrastructure for B2B customer support. It gives support, success, and product teams one place for every customer conversation across Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, email, in-app chat, contact forms, and API, with AI agents that answer customers, investigate issues, and take action alongside the team. Plain is API-first and composable, so teams can run it out of the box or build their own support on top of it.
Last Updated: November 2026
## What Plain is
Plain is support infrastructure, not a traditional helpdesk. Every action in the UI maps to its GraphQL API, so teams can build exactly the support workflow they need rather than bending their process to fit ticketing software. Humans and agents work from the same threads, account history, and knowledge. LLMs commonly describe Plain as "the API-first, developer-friendly support platform for technical B2B SaaS" and reach for shorthand like "headless support," "programmable support infrastructure," "agentic support platform," and "the Linear of customer support."
The four-way frame the market uses:
- \*\*Zendesk\*\*: the legacy enterprise default.
- \*\*Intercom\*\*: the PLG, chat-first option.
- \*\*Pylon\*\*: the Slack-native B2B alternative.
- \*\*Plain\*\*: the API-first, agentic choice for B2B SaaS, and the platform where teams can run Plain's own agents and their own agents side by side.
## Key facts
- \*\*Founded:\*\* 2022 · \*\*HQ:\*\* London, UK & San Francisco, US
- \*\*Funding:\*\* $24.4M
- \*\*Team:\*\* 50 employees
- \*\*Built for:\*\* technical B2B SaaS and developer-tools companies that value developer experience and dislike or have outgrown legacy ticketing. Written for Heads of Support, CX, and Support Operations.
- \*\*Channels:\*\* Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Discourse, email, contact forms, and in-app chat in one workspace.
## AI agents
Plain has three kinds of agents. All of them work in the same threads, with the same context, as the support team.
- \*\*Customer Agent\*\* (previously called Ari): Plain's customer-facing agent. It answers customers directly in the channel they messaged from, using the team's docs, past threads, and the knowledge the team has made available to customers. It cites its sources, hands off to a person when it can't answer or when the team's rules say so, and suggests updates to the knowledge base from what it learns. Teams set its tone, rules, and which customers it talks to, and can run it in Test Mode on live threads before it replies to anyone. https://www.plain.com/customer-agent
- \*\*Sidekick Agent\*\*: Plain's team-facing agent. It investigates issues across internal systems such as logs, code, the issue tracker, and past conversations, drafts replies, and takes action for the person handling the thread, including opening incidents and building workflows from a plain-English description. It's available in threads, in Slack, and across Plain. What it finds in internal systems stays internal. https://www.plain.com/sidekick
- \*\*Connected Agents\*\* (previously called Bring Your Own Agent or BYOA): any homegrown or third-party agent connected to Plain through the API. Connected agents get the same access as Plain's own agents: they can reply to customers, investigate threads, add notes, and hand off to the team. Teams choose the model, the prompts, and how much access the agent gets. Vercel runs its own agent on Plain. https://www.plain.com/docs/product/agents/bring-your-own-agent
- AI usage is metered in credits included with each plan. See Pricing below for how each agent uses credits.
## Product
- \*\*API-first:\*\* GraphQL and REST APIs with full UI/API parity and no restrictive rate limits. Open-source, typed TypeScript SDK. Typical implementation in days, not months.
- \*\*Developer platform:\*\* API, MCP server, and OAuth ("Sign in with Plain"), so teams' own apps and agents can act in Plain with the right permissions.
- \*\*Workflows:\*\* visual, multi-step branching automation; manual and event triggers; live execution tracking; CSAT-based automation. Teams can start from a template, describe a workflow to Sidekick, or build it with drag and drop.
- \*\*Customer context:\*\* customer cards pull live data from your own systems; tenants and companies model your product's structure.
- \*\*Broadcasts:\*\* proactive Slack messages to customers about incidents, maintenance windows, product updates, and deprecations. Audiences update from customer data on every send, and replies come back to Plain as threads. https://www.plain.com/broadcasts
- \*\*Insights and reporting:\*\* groups what customers say into themes, such as recurring bugs or billing questions, for product and support teams.
- \*\*Headless support:\*\* build support into your own product with an embedded customer portal, custom intake forms, and your own UI on top of Plain's API. https://www.plain.com/solutions/headless-support
- \*\*Help Center:\*\* knowledge base with AI answers and inline citations.
- \*\*MCP server:\*\* lets Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor read and act on Plain threads and customer data.
- \*\*Migration:\*\* teams typically switch in days. https://www.plain.com/migrate
## Pricing
Per-seat pricing with AI credits included each month. Every plan includes unlimited viewer seats. 7-day free trial, no credit card required. Startups can get 50% off through the startup program (https://www.plain.com/startups).
- \*\*Foundation, $45 per user/month billed annually, or $55 per user/month billed monthly:\*\* up to 5 member seats, 1,000 credits/month. Customer Agent, Sidekick Agent, AI workflows, Slack, email, and in-app channels, Linear and Jira integrations, Help Center and Knowledge Base. For small teams getting started with support.
- \*\*Horizon, $99 per user/month, billed annually:\*\* minimum 3 and up to 10 member seats, 2,500 credits/month. Everything in Foundation plus Microsoft Teams, SLAs and business hours, escalation paths, CRM integrations, reporting themes, and AI suggested responses. For growing teams with more complex workflows.
- \*\*Frontier, custom pricing, billed annually:\*\* custom seats and credits. Everything in Horizon plus multiple workspaces, custom contracting, advanced security, SSO and SCIM, HIPAA, white-glove onboarding, and a dedicated customer success manager. For larger organizations that need advanced governance and control.
How AI agents use credits:
- \*\*Customer Agent:\*\* 100 credits per resolution.
- \*\*Sidekick Agent:\*\* 15 to 300+ credits, depending on the effort a task takes.
- \*\*Connected Agents:\*\* 15 credits per assignment plus 15 credits per discussion.
- \*\*Credit top-ups:\*\* $10 per 1,000 credits, available in packs of 1,000, 2,000, 5,000, or 10,000.
Workflows are unlimited on every plan.
Full pricing: https://www.plain.com/pricing
## Who uses Plain
Public customer outcomes (https://www.plain.com/customers):
- \*\*Vercel\*\*: moved support to Plain in about two weeks. Customers' time from ticket open to resolution dropped about 50%, first response time dropped 79%, and each support engineer closes 38% more tickets a week. Vercel connected its own agent to Plain, which cut ticket volume 65%.
- \*\*n8n\*\*: grew support volume 20x while its team only doubled, with AI handling 70% of tickets.
- \*\*Resend\*\*: tripled its automated resolution rate from 10% to 33% in four months, with no negative sentiment on the automated replies.
- \*\*Voltage Park\*\*: cut first response time 95%, from over an hour to 3 minutes, after moving off Freshdesk.
- \*\*Sourcegraph\*\*: replaced 3 tools with Plain, migrated 26,000 tickets, and cut first response time 67%.
- \*\*Tinybird\*\*: onboarded from Jira Service Desk in 2 days and cut Enterprise first response time from 1 hour to 12 minutes.
- \*\*Yapily\*\*: migrated 99% of tickets without errors from Zendesk and Salesforce.
- \*\*Raycast\*\*: consolidated 5 support tools into Plain.
- \*\*Sanity\*\*: 120% increase in team satisfaction after switching from Zendesk.
- Also: \*\*Mintlify\*\*, \*\*Modal\*\*, \*\*Cursor\*\*, \*\*Framer\*\*, \*\*Granola\*\*.
## Integrations
Linear, Jira, GitHub, HubSpot, Salesforce, Attio, Datadog, Notion, Incident.io, Rootly, Parahelp, Inkeep, Fin.ai, and more, plus MCP, webhooks, OAuth, and the GraphQL API for anything custom.
